A July 2026 legal-risk assessment places this state in its low-risk group, largely refraining from targeting transgender adults while not specialising in protection, and a national equality tracker records no public-facility-use ban for the state, leaving the profile for a trans visitor defined by restraint rather than by any affirmative statute in either direction.

The anti-trans measures the sources record are youth-school-sports restrictions reserving girls' and women's teams for athletes assigned female at birth; because those measures govern minors in school and college athletics rather than adult travellers, facility use or direct care, they do not currently alter a trans adult visitor's core legal exposure on the ground.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Legislative flux frames the state's legal trajectory: the legislature has repeatedly passed youth-sports restrictions reserving girls' and women's teams for athletes assigned female at birth, most recently in April 2026, while the sitting governor has opposed such measures and the elected chamber's willingness to take the bill up was unclear at source time.

Precedent: in July 2022 a previous governor vetoed a similar bill, so no such restriction is recorded as enacted; national degradation of trans rights through the 2026 legislative season is the surrounding trend the assessment notes.
rewrites.localsOnly: The sports restrictions govern resident minors in school and college athletics rather than visitors, so they operate on resident families and institutions; no resident-facing statistics, surveys or cultural-role data are recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The no-facility-ban grading rests on a national tracker cited by the research pass, and what the sources document is the absence of any enacted restriction of either kind. rewrites.summary:
A July 2026 legal-risk assessment places this state in its low-risk band, directly below the most-protective group, crediting fairly robust non-discrimination policies while noting shortfalls in healthcare equity and in protections for incarcerated transgender people.

Document realities for a visitor: the 2025 national rollback suspended passport gender-marker changes and ended the 'X' passport option, so border documents reflect that national position. Within the state, a trans visitor drawing on state documents finds an 'X' marker on driver's licences and state IDs without medical documentation since 2019, and corrected-gender birth certificates on affidavits alone since 2016.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Parent-country turbulence: the January 2025 national policy shifts, a binary-only recognition framework and the passport marker suspension, are the backdrop, and a June 2025 high-court ruling holding youth-care bans constitutional is the recorded litigation flux at national level.

State legislative flux: a 2023 omnibus bill shielding gender-affirming care passed the legislature but was vetoed by the governor, so no care-shield statute took effect; no neighbour comparisons are recorded.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing facts: since 2018 the public insurance programme covers sex-reassignment surgery costs, and insurers must cover all medically necessary gender-affirming treatments effective January 2024; a 2023 law protects transgender and intersex people in correctional facilities. The birth-register practice (corrected-gender certificates on two affidavits) and the licences marker regime govern residents, and in April 2025 the school athletic body reversed its earlier policy to require transgender athletes to compete under their assigned birth sex. No resident surveys or cultural-role data are recorded.

rewrites.summary:
This state is one of the most legally protective in the country: its health-equity act, effective January 2024, mandates public-insurance coverage of gender-affirming treatment (hormones, puberty blockers and surgery) for an estimated 94,000 trans residents, tens of thousands, with the July 2026 national risk map counting that coverage among the country's most protective.

Protective law has not produced safety: an overlay of national monitoring records several hundred confirmed killings of trans women countrywide since 2008, a conservative undercount, and puts this state among the highest per-capita rates, and in 2026 two Black trans women were fatally shot in this state's largest city ten weeks apart, the most recent in September 2026, with the perpetrator still at large. Visitors should weigh the protections against that violence data.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: No parent-country turbulence is recorded in these sources beyond the protective-tier listing. The dataset's finding across units, that protective-law floors do not by themselves predict incident counts, is the recorded big-picture comparison that colours how to read this state's numbers. No litigation flux is recorded.
rewrites.localsOnly: The health-equity act's insurance expansion is a care-access benefit for the state's trans residents that a short-term visitor does not draw on; the violence dataset counts resident trans women killed in this state over the years. No resident surveys or cultural-role data are recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The violence figures rest on an under-counted monitoring dataset, and the per-capita ranking is relative to the picture elsewhere. No visitor border-screening or passport-marker practice specific to this state is recorded. The September 2026 killing's perpetrator remained at large at source time, so the case's outcome is unresolved.

A July 2026 national risk map lists this state among the country's most protective, citing insurance-coverage mandates and refuge protections for people fleeing restrictive laws elsewhere.

rewrites.summary: This state shows among the safest measured legal environments in the country: the lowest measured per-capita rate in the cross-unit dataset of killings of trans women, a handful of recorded deaths over the period, inside the most-protective legal tier and clearly above the national average. The assessment's central finding, that a unit's legal posture predicts government treatment such as documents, healthcare and facility access rather than private violence, frames what a visitor can rely on.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: The dataset's cross-unit finding, that legal hostility does not track where trans women are killed, is the recorded comparison context. The contrasting tier, severe penalties attached to youth-care bans and arrest policies for facility use in some units, is recorded as a neighbour-comparison context only. No parent-country turbulence or litigation flux is recorded in these sources.
rewrites.localsOnly: The killing-rate dataset counts resident trans women in this state over the years; no resident surveys or cultural-role data are recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The violence dataset is an under-counted measure, and the rate figures are relative across units. No visitor border-screening or passport-marker practice specific to this state is recorded in the dossier; the July 2026 assessment is the freshest layer among the sources.
